title: Cooling trial: association, disagreement, and a late correction

observations.transcript: Dr Lin: In our non-randomized trial of 24 machines, the median fell from 80 to 68 degrees Celsius after the fan and firmware were both changed. That is a 12-degree drop, not a 12-percent drop. We cannot attribute it to the fan alone.
Operator Reyes: I disagree that this establishes a general improvement. Two of the 24 machines overheated during high humidity; our usual dry-room tests missed that condition.
Dr Lin: The proposed mechanism is that more airflow removes heat faster. It is a hypothesis, not a measured explanation; the simultaneous firmware change confounds this comparison.
Reyes: If humidity exceeds 70 percent, keep the old cooling profile until the wet-room test passes. I am not recommending that every installation roll back.

Dr Lin: One correction before we close: the 68-degree median excludes the two overheated machines because their sensors stopped logging. The trial enrolled 24, but only 22 contributed to that median. This is not an all-machine success rate.

Reyes disputes general improvement: two of the 24 machines overheated in high humidity, a condition missed by dry-room tests.
